`GHUser.wrap(users, root)` already existed at that time (it's used elsewhere, e.g. `getFollows`), confirming this was an available utility that the author simply forgot to call in the new `wrapUp` override.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a23d6f60d57fab770e036948efe7f5973cedffb1

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `GHOrganization.java` using `git log --follow -p`, looking for when the `wrapUp(GHUser[] ...)` override inside `getMembers()`'s `PagedIterator` anonymous class was first introduced, since the fix commit simply adds the missing `GHUser.wrap(users, root)` call to an existing-but-empty method body.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `a23d6f6` ("Wed Jan 22 09:56:06 2014", author Ryan Kennedy) refactored `getMembers()` from an eager `AbstractList<GHUser>` (which called `root.getUser(shallow[index].getLogin())` per element, fully resolving each user) to a lazy `PagedIterable<GHUser>`/`PagedIterator<GHUser>` implementation. In doing so, it added an empty override:
```java
protected void wrapUp(GHUser[] page) {
}
```
This method is the designated hook for binding each page of raw deserialized `GHUser` objects to the `GitHub root` connection (via `GHUser.wrap(page, root)`), which the old implementation achieved implicitly by calling `root.getUser(...)`. The new code never wires up `root`, leaving returned `GHUser` objects without a connection to the API root, causing subsequent calls on those users to fail/NPE.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `GHUser.wrap(GHUser[], GitHub)` already existed at the time of `a23d6f6` and was used correctly elsewhere (e.g., `GHUser.getFollows()`), proving it was the established pattern the author should have used.
- Later commits (`2555620`, `e97fd9c`) modified this same method's signature/URL but preserved the empty `wrapUp` body verbatim, propagating the bug forward untouched.
- The fix commit `8fb3177` makes the minimal one-line change of inserting `GHUser.wrap(users, root);` into this exact empty body — a direct undo of the omission from `a23d6f6`.

I'm confident in this attribution since the diff mechanically traces back to a single empty method body first introduced in `a23d6f6`, with no intervening commit altering that specific logic.
